requirement_text.REQ-150:
Settle OQ-6 -- Lua 5.3 integer/float marshalling across VariableMerge and JSONB variable storage (blocks LUA-11). Decision-and-design requirement unblocking REQ-159/REQ-160. Decision 0014's OQ-6 says this must be settled once, centrally, before LUA-11 is expanded. Lua 5.3 distinguishes an integer subtype from a float subtype (3/2 is 1.5; integer division needs //) where LuaJIT 5.1 had a single number type. Letflow stores instance variables as JSONB and merges them through Letflow.Engine.VariableMerge -- a value written by a script, persisted, and read back must round-trip with a defined subtype.

Scope: write lib/letflow/design/req150-lua-number-marshalling.md that:
1. Establishes EMPIRICALLY, by running code against the adopted runtime (tv-labs/lua), how integers and floats cross the Elixir/Lua boundary in BOTH directions -- what Elixir term a Lua integer becomes, what a Lua float becomes, what a Lua script sees when handed an Elixir integer and an Elixir float, and whether the subtype survives a Jason.encode!/Jason.decode! round trip (JSONB storage behavior).
2. States one NORMATIVE RULE in a numbered section REQ-159/REQ-160 will cite by number: which Elixir type each Lua subtype maps to; what happens to a Lua float with no fractional part (does 2.0 persist as 2.0 or collapse to 2); what happens to an integer exceeding IEEE-754 exact range; what a script observes for a JSON null.
3. Names the exact module and function that will own the conversion (written once, not per host function).
4. Records that WASM-12 (REQ-171/REQ-172) requires the WASM host API to be semantically identical to Lua's -- this rule is what WASM must conform to, and the artefact must say so.

NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no host function implemented; no change to lib/letflow/engine/variable_merge.ex ships here.
